prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A battery bushing for a rechargeable battery has a mounting section and a contacting section. There is a torque ring, between the mounting section and the contacting section. The torque ring or the outer surface itself can be endowed with several indentations. The mounting section is configured to hold the battery bushing within a battery cover, into which it preferably is injection molded. The battery bushing is a hollow body, which has an outer wall and an inner wall. At the contacting section, the outer wall is conically shaped. At the mounting section, the outer wall has at least one circumferential projection forming a labyrinth. The inner wall comprises at least two sections. An upper section is approximately surrounded by the contacting section, and preferably has a conical shape. A lower section is approximately surrounded by the mounting section. The lower section preferably has (in a lateral sectional view) a concave shape. Between the upper section and the lower section, there may be an edge or a step.

The battery bushing for a rechargeable battery comprises a mounting section, a contacting section, and a torque ring arranged between the mounting section and the contacting section. The mounting section is designed to secure the battery bushing in a battery cover, preferably by embedding or fixing it in the battery cover during an injection-molding process. In this way, the bushing can be held reliably and permanently in position.

The battery bushing is formed as a hollow body having an outer wall and an inner wall. In the region of the contacting section, the outer wall is preferably conically shaped, enabling reliable electrical and mechanical contact with a corresponding connection element. In the region of the mounting section, the outer wall includes at least one circumferential projection. This projection may form part of a labyrinth structure, which improves anchoring of the battery bushing in the battery cover and can also enhance sealing between the bushing and the surrounding cover material.

The torque ring is positioned between the mounting section and the contacting section and may serve to absorb or transmit torque applied to the battery bushing during assembly or use. The torque ring and/or the outer surface of the battery bushing may include a plurality of indentations. These indentations can improve the mechanical interlock with the surrounding material of the battery cover, thereby increasing resistance to rotation and helping to prevent loosening of the bushing.

The inner wall of the hollow body includes an upper section and a lower section. The upper section is preferably conically shaped, while the lower section is preferably concavely shaped. An edge, shoulder, or step may be provided between the upper and lower sections, defining a transition region within the interior of the bushing. This internal geometry may facilitate connection to further battery components and can support reliable positioning, contacting, or sealing within the rechargeable battery assembly.
outputs.L4:
A rechargeable battery bushing is provided for establishing a reliable electrical and mechanical connection through a battery cover, particularly through an injection-molded plastic cover of a rechargeable battery housing. The bushing includes a body having a mounting section and a contacting section. The mounting section is configured to be embedded in, surrounded by, or otherwise securely integrated with the material of the battery cover during an injection-molding process. The contacting section is configured to provide an electrically conductive interface for connection to a battery pole, terminal element, cable connector, or other current-conducting component of the battery assembly.

To improve torque resistance and prevent rotation of the bushing relative to the molded battery cover, the bushing may include a torque ring arranged on or adjacent to the mounting section. The torque ring can be formed as an annular flange, rib, collar, or similar circumferential feature that engages the surrounding plastic material after molding. In some embodiments, the torque ring may include indentations, recesses, notches, or similar interruptions distributed around its circumference. These optional indentations allow the injection-molded cover material to flow into the indentations and form a positive-locking connection after solidification. As a result, the bushing is more effectively secured against twisting, loosening, or displacement when mechanical forces are applied during assembly or use.

The contacting section may include one or more conical contacting surfaces. These conical surfaces are shaped to cooperate with correspondingly shaped contact elements, thereby improving electrical contact pressure and alignment. A conical configuration can also facilitate assembly by guiding a mating component into the correct position. In addition, the bushing may be provided with circumferential projections, such as ribs, beads, shoulders, or annular protrusions. These projections increase the available engagement area between the bushing and the surrounding molded material and may further contribute to sealing, retention, and resistance to axial movement.

The bushing body is preferably formed as a hollow body. This hollow structure reduces material usage and weight while still providing sufficient mechanical strength and electrical conductivity. The hollow interior may also allow the bushing to receive or cooperate with additional battery components, such as a pole insert, fastening element, terminal connector, or sealing component. The inner wall of the hollow body may be provided with shaped sections, including tapered, stepped, curved, cylindrical, or conical wall regions. These shaped inner wall sections can improve the mechanical support of inserted components and can help distribute loads more evenly through the bushing during assembly and operation.

The mounting section may further include a mounting projection designed to form a labyrinth-like interface with the molded battery cover. This projection may extend radially, axially, or in a combined direction from the body of the bushing. When the battery cover material is molded around the projection, the resulting interface creates a tortuous path between the exterior and interior of the battery housing. Such a labyrinth structure improves sealing performance by making it more difficult for electrolyte, gas, moisture, or contaminants to pass along the interface between the bushing and the plastic cover. At the same time, the labyrinth configuration increases the mechanical interlocking surface, thereby improving retention of the bushing in the cover.

By combining the torque ring, optional circumferential indentations, conical contacting surfaces, circumferential projections, hollow body design, labyrinth-forming mounting projection, and shaped inner wall sections, the rechargeable battery bushing provides a robust and reliable component for integration into a battery cover. The design improves resistance to rotation and axial pull-out, enhances sealing at the cover interface, supports stable electrical contacting, and increases the mechanical durability of the battery assembly. This makes the bushing particularly suitable for rechargeable batteries that are exposed to vibration, thermal cycling, assembly torque, internal pressure, or other demanding operating conditions.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the main structural features of a battery bushing for a rechargeable battery in patent-style language.
counterfactuals.output:
A battery bushing for a rechargeable battery may be characterized as comprising a generally tubular conductive body configured to be mounted in an opening of a battery cover or lid and to receive or electrically connect with a battery terminal post. The bushing includes a central passage extending along a longitudinal axis, an outer peripheral surface adapted for sealing engagement with the surrounding cover material, and one or more flange, shoulder, rib, groove, or undercut formations arranged to mechanically anchor the bushing within the cover and inhibit electrolyte leakage.

In one embodiment, the bushing comprises a lead or lead-alloy insert having an upper terminal-contact portion, a lower post-receiving or post-connecting portion, and an intermediate sealing portion. The sealing portion may include annular projections or recesses to increase the bond area with molded polymeric cover material. The bushing may further define a tapered, stepped, or cylindrical bore for accommodating a terminal post, weld connection, press-fit connection, or cast-on connection.

The bushing may also include anti-rotation structure, such as flats, splines, knurls, ribs, or non-circular exterior regions, configured to resist rotational movement relative to the battery cover during attachment of an external cable connector. A sealing interface may be provided between the bushing and the cover, optionally enhanced by molded-in engagement, compression sealing, adhesive bonding, or an annular gasket. The bushing is thereby arranged to provide an electrically conductive path through the battery cover while maintaining mechanical retention and fluid-tight sealing for use in a rechargeable electrochemical cell or battery assembly.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical description of a rechargeable battery bushing, including its mounting section, contacting section, torque ring, hollow body walls, and sealing projections.
counterfactuals.output:
A rechargeable battery bushing is a conductive feedthrough component designed to pass current through a battery housing while maintaining a sealed interface. It includes a mounting section for securing the bushing to the battery cover or case, and a contacting section configured for electrical connection to an internal or external battery terminal.

The bushing has a hollow body defined by surrounding body walls, which may receive a terminal post, conductor, or fastening element. A torque ring is provided on or around the body to transmit installation or tightening torque without damaging the sealing interface. One or more sealing projections extend from the body walls or mounting section to engage the battery housing or a seal material, improving electrolyte-tight and gas-tight sealing during assembly and operation.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for a battery cover bushing that is injection molded into the cover and has conical contacting surfaces, a labyrinth projection, and stepped inner wall sections.
counterfactuals.output:
A battery cover bushing is provided for forming a sealed, mechanically stable terminal passage through an injection-molded battery cover. The bushing is configured to be placed in a mold and insert-molded directly into the battery cover so that the cover material surrounds and locks to the bushing during molding.

The bushing includes an annular bushing body having an opening for receiving a battery terminal or terminal post. On its outer surface, the bushing has conical contacting surfaces that cooperate with correspondingly molded cover material. These tapered surfaces improve seating of the bushing in the cover, distribute mechanical loads, and help resist loosening or displacement caused by terminal forces, thermal cycling, or vibration.

The bushing further includes at least one labyrinth projection extending outwardly from the bushing body. During injection molding, the cover material flows around this projection to form a tortuous interface path between the bushing and the surrounding plastic. The labyrinth geometry increases the sealing path length and helps prevent electrolyte, gas, or moisture from migrating along the bushing-cover interface. It also provides mechanical interlocking to improve pull-out resistance.

The inner wall of the bushing opening includes stepped wall sections of different diameters. These steps may define seating, guiding, or sealing regions for a terminal post, insert, or sealing element. The stepped configuration can also accommodate different functional zones, such as a lead-through portion, a compression or bonding region, and a terminal support region.

In one embodiment, the bushing is made of a metal compatible with a battery terminal material, such as lead, lead alloy, copper alloy, or another conductive or corrosion-resistant material. The bushing is positioned in an injection mold for a battery cover, and plastic cover material is injected around the bushing so that the conical contacting surfaces and labyrinth projection become embedded in the molded cover. After molding, the bushing is permanently integrated into the battery cover and provides a sealed passage for electrical connection between an internal battery element and an external terminal.

This construction provides a robust battery cover interface with improved sealing, enhanced mechanical retention, and accurate positioning of the terminal passage. The conical contacting surfaces assist in force transfer and alignment, the labyrinth projection improves leak resistance by creating a tortuous sealing path, and the stepped inner wall sections provide functional surfaces for receiving and supporting terminal components.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: In plain technical terms, explain the design of a battery bushing having an outer conical contacting section, circumferential mounting projections, and an inner wall divided into upper and lower sections.
counterfactuals.output:
A battery bushing is a conductive insert used to pass current through and seal into a battery cover, typically around a terminal post. In plain technical terms, the described design has three main features:

1. **Outer conical contacting section**  
   The outside of the bushing includes a tapered, cone-shaped contact area. This conical shape helps it fit tightly into a matching opening or sealing area in the battery cover. As the bushing is pressed or molded into place, the taper improves mechanical wedging, electrical contact, and sealing. It can also help guide assembly and reduce looseness between the bushing and surrounding material.

2. **Circumferential mounting projections**  
   Around the outside surface of the bushing are ring-like projections or ribs. These projections extend around the circumference of the part. Their purpose is to lock the bushing into the plastic or molded battery cover. During molding or insertion, the cover material surrounds or engages these ribs, resisting pull-out, twisting, and leakage paths. They also increase the surface area for sealing between the bushing and the cover.

3. **Inner wall divided into upper and lower sections**  
   The inside of the bushing has a passage for receiving or surrounding a battery terminal post. This inner wall is divided into two functional sections:
   - An **upper inner wall section**, which may be shaped to receive a connector, terminal, or post portion near the top of the battery.
   - A **lower inner wall section**, which may have a different diameter, taper, thickness, or surface profile to fit the internal battery post or improve casting, welding, or sealing.

Together, these features create a bushing that can be securely fixed in the battery cover, provide a reliable conductive path to the battery terminal, and maintain a tight seal against electrolyte leakage and gas escape. The conical exterior improves seating, the circumferential projections improve mechanical retention, and the two-section inner wall allows the bushing to interface with different parts of the terminal structure.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
